result:
I computed all eight answers and saved them to `/work/answer.json`. I recalculated a, b and f with a separate SQL query and got the same numbers.

| Item | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment in Q3 by net sales | `enterprise`, 298,360,807 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order in Q3 | 244 |
| c. Top category in Q3 by net sales | `sw`, 294,263,064 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-08` (299,188,029 KRW) |
| e. Customer with the largest refunds in Q3 | `u48@ex.com` (2,450,000 KRW, no tie) |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders in Q3 | 237 |
| g. Average net sales per paid order in Q3 | 669,919 KRW (over 1,228 orders) |
| h. September vs August growth | −12.0% (exact value −12.0048…%) |

**How I handled the data:**
- I converted UTC to KST by adding 9 hours. Q3 is KST 2025-07-01 00:00 up to, but not including, 2025-10-01 00:00. This moves 216 orders placed near quarter boundaries into a different quarter than UTC would.
- Segment labels had stray spaces and mixed case (`' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, `'SMB'`). After trimming and lowercasing they collapse to three: consumer, enterprise and smb.
- 45 email addresses belong to more than one account. In b, e and f each email counts as one customer.
- I found no refunds without a matching order line, no refunds larger than the quantity sold, no duplicate refunds and no orphan rows.

**One judgement call (affects a):** 32 of the shared emails have accounts in different segments. I credited each order to the segment of the account that placed it. If instead each person gets one segment (that of their lowest-numbered account), the top segment is still `enterprise`, but its net sales become 289,180,291 KRW.

STATUS: DONE
